subject: unreal
note: Where every volatile Unreal SDK fact comes from. The pack prose must not restate a name this file can derive; it names the recipe, and extract_surface.py runs it. The source checkout is per-machine and is never recorded here. Unlike Unity, the plugin is the repository root rather than a package inside it, so package_root is empty.

modules.why: The modules the plugin declares. A module missing from the pack is a whole surface the writer is blind to, and a wrong module name is a build error the reader cannot diagnose.

types.why: Every type the plugin declares in a header. This settles whether a name a page uses is real. Includes forward declarations, which is the safe direction: a name declared and never defined is not surface either way.

public_types.why: Types under Public/ are the ones another module - and therefore a reader's project - can use. This is the set a scripting reference documents.

components.why: The components a reader adds to an Actor. Narrowed by name because a C++ header declares the component beside its state enum and helper structs, and those are not components.

blueprint_labels.why: A Blueprint node's label and its C++ name differ constantly - UConvaiChatbotComponent shows as "Convai Chatbot". Telling a reader to search for the C++ name sends them looking for a node that is not there.

actions.why: Character action tasks, which the actions pages name individually.

must_not_exist_why: Names a writer coming from the Unity SDK would reasonably guess, because Unity's equivalent is ConvaiCharacter, plus a type the pack already warns about: EConvaiMoveTarget was removed in the Movement Points rework. Listing it here is what makes check_site.py catch it on a published page, rather than leaving the warning as a sentence only a writer who reads the pack will see.
documented_sets_why: Small enough that every member matters. A missing module is a whole documented surface nobody wrote down.
coverage_sets_why: Reported as a single ratio rather than one warning per name. The types set holds hundreds of internal helpers, so it is deliberately not a coverage set.
symbol_prefixes_why: Unreal's type prefixes, narrowed to ours. Without the Convai part this would flag every engine type a page legitimately names, such as UActorComponent.
historical_pages_why: Pages whose job is to say what changed, plus the v1 guides kept for readers who have not migrated. A retired type name on one of these is correct, not drift.
coverage_ignore_prefixes_why: Sample and tutorial asset names that appear on pages but are outside the shipped plugin surface.
section_why: Where this subject's pages live in the documentation repository. Declared rather than inferred from the pack name: core-service's pages are under api-reference, and guessing reported its own exemplars as borrowed from another subject.
